aboutMore: ok second paragraph, the part nobody asked for ;) i deliver for Sal's Pizza & Subs four nights a week in my grandpa's old Buick (the tape deck is stuck on usher's confessions). 214 deliveries so far and i know every porch on my route by name. i also take a speech class tuesdays at the community college, where i got an A for 'how to tie a tie' (demonstrated on Sal. he said 'do not wink at the customers.' i said 'sir i would never.' i have winked at 3 customers). i'm saving up to take my nonna to see the ocean. she's 81 and has never seen it. lake erie doesn't count, she says. don't tell her. she thinks the money is for Axe.

blog.title: 214 pizzas: a gentleman's field report
blog.body: things i have learned delivering for Sal's, in no order. 1) people say thank you to the pizza and not to the guy. that's fine. i'm the guy who walks it to the door. 2) the Delgados on Brookline always have wheel of fortune on and mr delgado will not let me leave until i guess a letter. thursday it was a whole PHRASE and i got it with 3 letters showing. mrs delgado said 'see, he's sharp.' i got a cookie. 3) a 5 year old in a cape opened the door and said 'password?' i said 'hey ;)' and he said 'wrong' and shut it. his dad came out and tipped $6. the kid was right. 4) i did NOT wink at a single customer on tuesday and nothing bad happened. nobody even noticed. that's the scary part. 5) best tip ever: a hand towel. long story. i keep it in the Buick. it's the nicest thing i own. ok going back out, i have a large pepperoni for a lady named Gloria and i feel like she's the one ;) (she's 70) (it's a pepperoni feeling)

blog.title: THE CODE (a gentleman's handbook, 9 rules, laminated at the library)
blog.body: rule 1: walk on the street side. always. nobody asked. do it anyway. rule 2: hold the door even if they're 40 feet away. they will run. it's fine, you just made someone's day slightly more athletic. rule 3: no winks at funerals, hospitals, church or the dmv (i learned this the hard way. i won't say which one). rule 4: carry a second capri sun. someone is thirsty. it's never who you think. rule 5: if she says no, say 'thanks for being honest' and MEAN it. this took me until number 31 to learn and until number 40 to actually do. rule 6: walk people to their car after dark. not as a move. as a rule. rule 7: text back. everybody. even chad (his texts are just the word GO). rule 8: never say a word about another guy's girl. kayla and bryan are THE couple and i say 'hey' with no wink. rule 9: compliment the mom. 'this is a beautiful house, ma'am' has gotten me fed 3 times. there is no rule 10. still researching.

blog.title: sunday at nonna's
blog.body: nonna rosa's gravy takes 6 hours and i'm only allowed to stir, taste and be quiet. she's 81. she has never once said no to me, so she's not in the 54, she's her own category: 1 for 1 forever. today i told her i'm 0 for 54 and she put down the spoon. she NEVER puts down the spoon. she said 'and how many of them did you leave crying.' i said none. she said 'how many did you thank.' i said all of them. she said 'so you are 54 for 54, Antonio. at being a man.' then she told me grandpa proposed with a dandelion he found growing out of the sidewalk outside the church, in march, the only flower in ohio. she said 'i said yes because he was soaked from the rain and he was still asking nicely.' i have been holding a wooden spoon for 20 minutes. the gravy is probably fine. she says it's never not fine.

blog.title: THE LEDGER AUDIT: what 54 'no's actually said (a study)
blog.body: i went through the notebook (yes there's a notebook) and sorted every no by type. 31 were 'no thanks' (polite). 9 were 'i have a boyfriend' (respect). 6 were silence (the vending machine is in this category. so is the mannequin.) 4 were laughs, but the nice kind, the 'oh, tony' kind. 2 were 'tony. no.' (fair.) 1 was 'ask me again in a year' (it has been 9 months. i have a calendar.) 1 was a girl who said she'd say yes but she was moving to phoenix, which i am counting as a maybe. total: 54. number of mean ones: 0. zero. i read that twice. 54 people were kind to me while telling me no. that is a really good town. akron, i love you. i'm still going to say hey ;) but from now on i'm going to say it like i mean it.

none. but every dog on the east side knows my whistle (9 dogs, 1 of them bit me, it was a misunderstanding)

that number 55 says yes and i forget everything i practiced. there's a note card in my collar. it says 'ask about their day'

parallel parking. any car, any spot, one try. nobody has ever asked me. it's my second best skill after winking and my first best skill after everything else

garlic knots at 9 PM. second place: nonna's kitchen. third place: Axe Phoenix (it's complicated) ;)

the end of Rudy. a commercial about a dog and a soldier. and then i remembered the hand towel guy

head of the door at teen nite (it's a napkin) (it's a title). after that, a guy who delivers the pizza AND stays for the party
advice for younger tony:
carry a second capri sun and learn to say 'thanks for being honest.' you will need both by number 2
describe yourself in one sentence:
i'm 0 for 54, i hold every door, and i know 31 porches by name, and honestly that's a better batting average than it sounds ;)

dms: {you} a girl took her pizza at the door tonight, paid, and said 'you're the guy who wrote on my friend's wall.' i said 'guilty ;)' and she said 'she says you're really nice.' i'm 0 for 54 but i think i might be 1 for 1 on 'really nice.' it's a new column. i'm starting a spreadsheet

{you} i went to tyler's 'collar summit' on saturday (his driveway, two chairs, a cooler). he pops 2, i pop 1 plus the axe. coach reilly judged. the verdict: 'all collars are valid. tony, do not wink at the judge.' i have never been so accepted or so busted in the same minute

the tape deck ate usher again. day 11. i know the songs in order including the part where the tape stretches. i call that one 'the tony remix.' the Buick and i are in a relationship and it's going well

the 10th dog on my route, a beagle named biscuit, rolled over for me in the middle of somebody's lawn. his owner said 'he never does that.' i'm 10 for 10 on dogs. i've started a column. it's the best column in the notebook
quick question, no line, no wink: how's your day. i'm serious. i'll wait. i delivered through a blizzard in march, i can wait for a reply

cousin vince called. he's making me 'head of the door' at teen nite. i said what does that mean. he said 'you say hey to everybody and count them.' {you} that's my whole life. the title is on a napkin. i have a clipboard. i'm saying hey to 42 people tonight and winking at none of them

sal (the owner) gave me a 50 cent raise today. he said 'you smile at the door. nobody smiles at the door.' i said 'sir it's a reflex.' he said 'keep the reflex.' i sat in the Buick for a full minute. it's a good Buick
i signed malten's guestbook. took 4 tries because i kept typing 'hey ;)' as my message. final version: 'nice site.' then a wink. growth is slow but it's happening

the lady at the corner store knows my order: two capri suns, one for 'destiny.' tonight she gave me a third and said 'this one's for you, hon.' {you} i got emotional over a juice pouch in a parking lot

i read malten's 'Why do I create?' on my break in the Buick with a large pepperoni cooling on the seat. i think people create stuff to say 'hey' without having to say hey. i've been saying hey with a wink for years. maybe a pizza is a hey. maybe a speech is a hey. maybe this whole site is just a hey. i'm gonna be quiet for a minute. (one minute.) ;)
